issues.body: read_output accepts any Python float, including `nan`. In validate_float, `abs(nan - r) > bound` is false, so an actual output containing NaN for every expected vertex passes validation. This makes the load-bearing correctness gate unsound and is not covered by the gate self-test.
issues.fix_hint: Reject non-finite reference and actual values with `math.isfinite` before applying the tolerance comparison, and add self-tests proving NaN and both infinities are rejected.
issues.title: PageRank validator accepts NaN as a valid result

issues.body: For both sparq and competitor legs, the captured runner log is printed before gate_and_record is called. Those logs contain `metric_us algo=...`, so a red validation result still exposes its timing. This directly contradicts the stated invariant that validation occurs before any timing is reported and that a red row has no timing printed.
issues.fix_hint: Parse and retain timing internally, run validation first, and only print the timing/log lines after a successful gate. On mismatch, print diagnostics with all timing lines filtered or never emitted.
issues.title: The harness prints algorithm timings before validation

issues.body: The adapter correctly labels igraph PageRank as converged, but run.sh passes the same Graphalytics fixed-sweep reference used for sparq into gate_and_record. No converged reference is generated or selected. The comments and README claim the igraph row is gated against a converged reference, so the implemented competitor comparison is incomplete and ordinarily produces a semantic mismatch rather than the documented validated row.
issues.fix_hint: Either generate and clearly identify an independent converged oracle for the igraph row, or classify igraph PageRank as an incomparable feature/semantic gap and remove the claim that it is validated against a converged reference. Do not compare it to the fixed-sweep output.
issues.title: igraph PageRank is validated against the fixed-iteration reference, not a converged reference

issues.body: The N-Triples scratch path is always `/tmp/sparq-graphalytics-{name}.nt` and File::create follows existing symlinks. Concurrent runs of the same dataset can truncate or read each other's file, invalidating results; on a shared machine, an attacker can pre-create a symlink and cause the runner to overwrite another writable file. The drop cleanup does not prevent either problem.
issues.fix_hint: Create a private unique temporary file/directory atomically (for example with tempfile, or create_new plus a securely unique name and restrictive permissions), keep its handle/path scoped to the run, and add a concurrency-oriented test or check.
issues.title: Predictable shared /tmp file permits races and symlink overwrite

verdict.summary: The harness has several correctness defects in its load-bearing validation and reporting paths. Most seriously, PageRank validation accepts NaN values, timings are printed before validation despite the central validate-before-report claim, and the igraph PageRank leg is checked against the wrong reference semantics. The Rust runner also uses a predictable shared temporary pathname, creating concurrency corruption and symlink-overwrite risk.
